summary: Each round players place Ambassador tokens on a shared Senate grid, deciding every time whether that token funds a Major Project or casts a vote on pending legislation, with single-use spaces creating constant blocking tension. It rewards funding-heavy play and shifts noticeably by player count, playing best with 4 and feeling weaker at 2-3.
praised: The Senate placement/voting dilemma and the blocking tension it creates ('plenty of tension on the Senate board')
High production quality with clear player-progress tracking
Plays best and most interactively at higher player counts
criticised: Funding tokens are disproportionately used by winners (~62% per one reviewer's tally), making optimal play somewhat formulaic
Secondary planet-development tracks feel 'pedestrian' and repetitive
Balance shifts noticeably by player count, weaker at 2-3 players
Most Major Projects reliably complete, reducing end-game suspense
Theme described by one reviewer as fairly tacked-on

interaction.kind: Shared worker placement, blocking, and voting
interaction.detail: Most of the game state is communal rather than private: the Senate grid, Major Project tracks, and passed laws are all shared, and single-use action spaces mean players directly block each other's options. Voting on legislation also lets players collectively alter shared scoring conditions that affect everyone.

sources: prestige earned from actions each round
end-of-game majority/influence bonuses in the federation
scoring.how_you_win: Across 5 fixed rounds you place workers to develop your delegation and earn prestige, and whoever has accumulated the most prestige (including final influence bonuses) after year 5 is admitted to the federation as the winner.
